title: Truncating the halting-output probability
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let $x$ be an input word, and let $B$ be a natural number. Suppose that for every natural number $K$, the sum of the probabilities that the run on $x$ has not halted after $t$ choices, over all $t<K$, is at most $B$. Then for every Boolean word $v$ and every natural number $t'$, the probability that a uniformly random choice word of length $t'$ makes the machine halt with output $v$ is at most the corresponding probability for choice words of length $100B$, plus $1/100$.
